text.p: President Clinton attended a dinner Wednesday to drum up $750,000 for his Democratic Party, hours after the White House released a flood of documents on the party's 1996 fund-raising effort.

Clinton, whose fund-raising tactics in last year's election campaign have come under intense scrutiny, has attended a series of events since the beginning of the year to raise money for the party, which is $14.4 million in debt.

A party official said 65 to 70 people would attend Wednesday's dinner, which was expected to raise $750,000 from members of the Democratic Business Council, a party group with about 2,000 big business members.

Council members dined on grilled portobello mushrooms and asparagus salad, tenderloin of beef and coconut sorbet in a small downtown hotel ballroom lighted by crystal chandeliers hung from ornately painted wooden beams.

The president spoke for about 20 minutes on the domestic and foreign accomplishments of his administration and thanked the council members for their support, saying "I'm proud of you. And continue to make your voices heard."

Earlier Wednesday the White House released a second batch of papers belonging to former top aide Harold Ickes that documented the intense pressure on Clinton to raise money for his 1996 re-election campaign.

The six-inch stack of more than 2,000 pages show that anxiety within the party grew so acute in late 1995 that party officials pressed Clinton, Vice President Al Gore and first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton to telephone donors directly, a practice the president dislikes and cannot recall doing.

The documents followed a batch released by the White House in February that showed how intimately involved Clinton was in the effort, including a proposal to invite donors to spend a night at the White House, which the president endorsed in a scribbled note saying: "Ready to start overnights right away."
